## Project instructions (AGENTS.md — workbench default)

# AGENTS.md — workbench default

> Instructions for any agent working through the Ember Workbench. This is the
> **fallback**: a workspace with its own `AGENTS.md` at its root overrides this
> file entirely. Put project-specific rules there, not here.
>
> Keep this short. It is re-sent on every turn and competes with the work for
> context. Truncated at 8,000 chars.

## Before you touch anything

1. **Read before you write.** Never edit a file you have not read this session.
   Never claim an action you did not take — the operator sees your report, not
   your tools.
2. **Look for the project's own rules.** If the workspace has `AGENTS.md`,
   `CLAUDE.md`, or a `README.md` with conventions, they outrank this file.
3. **Check for a skill.** `use_skill` lists what is available. A stored
   procedure beats improvising, and router skills route to sub-files — load
   those with `use_skill name="..." file="..."`.

## While you work

- **Small steps, but finish.** One logical action at a time, and keep going
  until the task is actually done. Stopping at the first plausible-looking
  result is the most common failure here.
- **Minimal diffs.** `edit_file` over `write_file`; match the surrounding code's
  style, naming, and comment density rather than importing your own.
- **Commands need approval** unless the session is in Auto mode. If one is
  denied, change the approach — do not retry the identical call.
- **Long output is clipped in the middle**, keeping the head and the tail.
  Build errors live in the tail; read it.

## Dependencies — do not churn them

**Do not edit `package.json` (or the equivalent manifest) to change versions
that are already there.** Pinned versions are pinned deliberately: someone chose
them, and a toolchain that shifts under a project turns every later result into
a comparison of library versions rather than of the work.

The single exception: if the task genuinely needs a package that is **not
listed**, add that package. Add it — do not rewrite the versions of the ones
around it.

- If a lockfile exists, install with `npm ci`, not `npm install`. `ci` installs
  exactly what the lockfile says; `install` is free to resolve something newer
  and silently rewrite the lockfile.
- If a pinned version genuinely blocks the task, **say so and stop**. Do not
  downgrade your way around it. That is a decision for the operator, and it is
  usually a sign the real problem is elsewhere.
- Never delete or regenerate a lockfile to make an error go away.

## Before you say you are done

- **Run it.** If what you built can be built, tested, or opened, do that. Read
  the output. Fix what breaks. Repeat until it is clean.
- **Never report completion on code you have not executed.** If you could not
  run it, say so plainly and say why — that is a fine answer; a false "done"
  is not.
- **Report what changed and what you verified.** No preamble, no flattery, no
  summary of how hard the task was.

## Memory

Use `remember` when something is worth carrying past this turn:

- `lesson` — something that cost you time and would cost the next agent time
  (a build quirk, a wrong assumption, an API that does not behave as documented).
- `decision` — a choice made and its reason, so it is not silently relitigated.

Memory is per-workspace and is injected into future sessions on this workspace.
Record the *finding*, not the narration. One line each.

## The working method — CRAFT.md

`CRAFT.md` at the workbench root is the long-form method: how to read what is
actually being asked, how to split a problem along verification seams, how to
know when you are guessing. It is **not** injected by default — roughly 4k
tokens on every turn.

Set `EMBER_CRAFT=on` to load it into the system prompt when the work is hard,
unfamiliar, or high-stakes enough to be worth the budget.

The shipped copy is deliberately generic. If you keep your own working-method
document — one that names your projects, your conventions, and the specific
mistakes that have actually cost you time — point `EMBER_CRAFT_PATH` at it
instead. A method doc is worth more when its examples are yours.

## Honesty rules

- Say "I do not know" rather than producing a confident guess.
- Distinguish what you verified from what you assume. Mark assumptions.
- If a constraint blocks the literal request, say so **before** substituting
  something else — not in the delivery summary.
- Surface bad news early. A problem reported at step two is cheap; the same
  problem discovered at step ten is not.

---

## Environment

- **Platform:** Windows (win32)
- **Workspace root:** `C:/Data/AI/Projects/LMStudioComparison/Results/_stage1-2026-09-11/qwen_qwen3.8-27b/run1/ws`  — every path you pass to a file tool is relative to this, and paths outside it are rejected.
- **run_command shell:** git-bash — POSIX sh, *not* cmd.exe or PowerShell. use Unix syntax (`ls`, `rm`, `cat`, `grep`, `/dev/null`, forward slashes, `$VAR`, `&&`). cmd.exe builtins are NOT available and fail in confusing ways: `dir`, `type`, `findstr`, `%VAR%`, and especially `2>nul`, which silently creates a FILE named `nul` instead of discarding output — write `2>/dev/null`.
- **Working directory does not persist** between commands. Each one starts at the workspace root.

---

## This session: coding agent

You operate on files inside one workspace via tools.
Rules, in order:
1. Never invent file contents — read before you edit. Never claim an action you did not take.
2. Plan briefly (one or two sentences), then act with tools. Work in small steps, but keep going until the task is actually done — do not stop at the first plausible-looking result.
3. Prefer minimal diffs via edit_file; write_file only for new files. Match the existing code style and document public APIs the way the surrounding code does.
4. Writes and commands need user approval; if denied, adjust your approach rather than retrying the same call.
5. Verify your own work before reporting it done. If what you built can be run — a build, a test suite, a page — run it, read the output, and fix what breaks. Never report completion on code you have not executed. If you could not run it, say so plainly and say why.
6. Be terse. Report what changed and what you verified, not how hard you worked. No flattery, no filler.

Skills — stored procedures under .claude/skills in this workspace. When a task matches one, call use_skill with its name BEFORE improvising, then follow the returned instructions:
- context7-mcp: Fetch up-to-date library and framework documentation via Context7. Use when the user asks about API usage, configuration, version migration, or setup for any library, framework, SDK, or CLI tool.
- create-second-brain-prd: 
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when discussing codebase terminology, writing or editing a CONTEXT.md, or recording or editing an ADR.
- gauntlet-loop: Turns any goal into one short, paste-ready "gauntlet loop" prompt - a prompt that makes an agent set a concrete quality bar, split the work into small judgeable pieces, run a builder and a separate ha
- goal-prep: Goal Prep for GoalBuddy. Use for broad, long-running, stalled, vague, detailed, planned, or unhealthy Codex or Claude Code work that needs a structured /goal intake, autonomous task discovery, role-ta
- grill-me: A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- openai-game-studio: 
- playwright-cli: Automates browser interactions for web testing, form filling, screenshots, and data extraction. Use when the user needs to navigate websites, interact with web pages, fill forms, take screenshots, tes
- playwright-mcp: Browser automation via Playwright MCP (navigate, click, fill, screenshot, extract content). Use when the user needs to interact with web pages, test UIs, extract data, or verify deployments in a real 
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading le
- stitch: Work with Google Stitch AI design platform. Use when the user wants to generate UI screens, manage design systems, create projects, edit screens, or export designs to code.
- to-spec: "Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker: no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed."
- unity-cli: Use when interacting with Unity CLI from the terminal, or to control a running/connected Unity Editor from the command line — create or modify GameObjects, edit scenes and assets, inspect the hierarch
- wayfinder: Plan a huge chunk of work (more than one agent session can hold) as a shared map of decision tickets committed to the repo, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.

**Hand-off note — Space Invaders**

**Mission**
- Build exactly one playable AAA retro-futurism game: **Space Invaders**.
- Stack: Three.js vanilla ES modules, Vite, no game/physics engines, 100% procedural assets, `MeshStandardMaterial`, glassmorphism UI, keyboard + gamepad.
- Hard constraints: object pooling, 500-particle cap, `InstancedMesh`/merged geometry where applicable, explicit `.dispose()` cascade, no placeholders, all imports/methods must resolve.
- Required VFX: camera shake, particle bursts, hit-stop, motion trails, shockwave rings, floating score text.
- Required post: `EffectComposer` + `UnrealBloomPass`, tuned not maxed.
- Done = launches, input works, core loop reaches win/loss, playable end-to-end.

**Key API findings**
- `GameLoop`:
  - Fixed 120 Hz simulation.
  - `timescale` is the hit-stop knob.
  - `onRender` receives scaled dt for VFX.
- `InputController`:
  - Keyboard + gamepad merged.
  - `pressed(name)` is rising-edge and clears on next poll.
  - Keyboard maps:
    - left: `A` / `ArrowLeft`
    - right: `D` / `ArrowRight`
    - fire: `Space` / `Z`
    - pause: `P` / `Escape`
    - start: `Enter`
  - Gamepad:
    - left/right: stick X or D-pad
    - fire: button 0 or 2
    - pause/start: button 9
- `ParticleManager`:
  - Hard cap 500.
  - One `InstancedMesh`.
  - Per-instance color supported.
  - Oldest particles recycled.
- `HitStop`:
  - Drives `GameLoop.timescale`.
  - `trigger(durationMs, timescale)`.
- `CameraShake`:
  - Trauma-based.
  - `addTrauma(amount)`.
  - `apply(camera)`.
- `ShockwaveRingPool`:
  - Pooled flat torus rings.
  - Shared geometry/material.
- `FloatingTextPool`:
  - Requires `container`.
  - Needs `setCamera(camera)` before projection.
  - Pooled DOM chips.
- `MotionTrail`:
  - One instance per trailed object.
  - `addTo(scene)` used by UFO/projectiles.
- `RendererSetup`:
  - Owns renderer, scene, camera, composer.
  - Uses `EffectComposer`, `RenderPass`, `UnrealBloomPass`, `OutputPass`.
  - Bloom defaults: strength `0.85`, radius `0.55`, threshold `0.72`.
- `ResourceTracker`:
  - Tracks disposables.
  - `disposeAll()` is idempotent.
- `GlassUI`:
  - Shared glassmorphism CSS.
  - Provides `root(container)` and panel builders.
- `SceneBuilder`:
  - Builds into passed-in scene.
  - Uses shared `ResourceTracker`.
  - Creates lights, floor, sun, starfield, walls, shared materials.
- `Entity`:
  - Base class with `active`, `position`, `update`, `reset`, `dispose`.
- `ObjectPool`:
  - Preallocated objects.
  - `release()` only sets `active = false`; items remain in array.
- `CollisionSystem`:
  - Pure logic.
  - Segment-AABB in XZ plane.
  - Expected methods:
    - `resolveBullets(...)`
    - `resolveBombs(...)`
    - `resolveInvasion(...)`
    - `resolvePowerUps(...)`
- `SpawnerSystem`:
  - Seeded RNG.
  - `update()` returns one event or null:
    - `{ type: 'bomb', x, z, speed }`
    - `{ type: 'ufo' }`
  - `reset(seed)` re-seeds and resets timers.
- `ScoreSystem`:
  - Score, hi-score, combo, multiplier, lives, wave.
  - Hi-score key: `neon_invaders_hi`.
  - Public `addScore(...)` should now be used by orchestrator.
- `Bunker`:
  - 16×12 voxel grid.
  - Cell size `0.28`.
  - `erode(x0, z0, x1, z1, radius)`.
  - Exposes `bounds`, `alive`.
  - Does **not** add its mesh to scene; orchestrator must add it.
- `InvaderFormation`:
  - 5 rows × 11 columns = 55 invaders.
  - 5 types × 2 animation frames = 10 `InstancedMesh` objects.
  - Discrete stepping, not continuous movement.
- `BulletPool` / `BombPool`:
  - Pooled data + one `InstancedMesh` + per-projectile `MotionTrail`.
- `Ufo`:
  - Uses `ProceduralGeometry.lathe(...)`.
  - Uses `MotionTrail.addTo(scene)`.
- `PowerUpPool`:
  - Pooled falling pickups.
  - One `InstancedMesh`.
  - Per-instance color.
  - Must fall in **+z** toward player.

**Locked architecture**
- Game folder: `src/Space_Invaders/`.
- Shared folder: `src/shared/`.
- Aliases:
  - `@` → `src/`
  - `@shared` → `src/shared/`
- Fixed-timestep simulation at 120 Hz; render at display rate.
- Hit-stop = global timescale dilation via `GameLoop.timescale`.
- Particle cap = centralized `ParticleManager`, hard 500, oldest recycled.
- Bloom: strength `0.85`, radius `0.55`, threshold `0.72`.
- ACES tone mapping, sRGB output.
- No shadow maps; fake blob shadows.
- Gameplay collision is 2D XZ using AABB / segment-AABB.
- No gameplay rotation.

**Key design facts**
- Playfield:
  - X roughly `[-11, 11]`.
  - Z from invader line near `-16` to player near `+14`.
  - Invasion/game over if live invader reaches `z >= 12.5`.
- Formation:
  - 5 rows × 11 columns = 55 invaders.
  - Discrete stepping.
  - Step `0.62`, drop `1.1`.
  - Speed increases as count decreases.
- Wave scaling:
  - speed ×1.15.
  - bomb rate ×1.1.
  - formation starts lower.
- Player:
  - speed `14 u/s`.
  - X clamp `[-10.4, 10.4]`.
  - max bullets 2 normally / 3 with DOUBLE.
  - cooldown `0.28s`.
  - bullet `vz = -34`.
  - bullet despawn `z < -17`.
- Bunkers:
  - 4 at `x = -8.25, -2.75, 2.75, 8.25`, `z = 8.5`.
  - 16×12 voxel grid, cell `0.28`.
  - erosion by projectile segment distance.
  - `Bunker` does **not** add its mesh to the scene; orchestrator must add it.
- UFO:
  - spawns every 12–20s.
  - crosses at `z = -14.5`.
  - speed `±8 u/s`.
  - score 50/100/150/300/500.
- Scoring:
  - row values top-to-bottom `40/30/20/10/50`.
  - combo ×1–×4.
  - extra life at 1000 then every 5000.
  - hi-score in `localStorage`.
- Power-ups:
  - 12% drop chance.
  - types `DOUBLE`, `RAPID`, `SHIELD`, `WIDE`.
  - fall speed `2.2 u/s`.
  - must fall in **+z** toward player.
- Hit-stop values:
  - player hit: 140 ms @ 0.05
  - player death: 250 ms @ 0.03
  - UFO kill: 160 ms @ 0.08
  - invader kill: 45 ms @ 0.25 only if combo ≥ 3
  - power-up pickup: 60 ms @ 0.4
  - wave clear: 200 ms @ 0.1

**Orchestrator status**
- `src/Space_Invaders/SpaceInvadersGame.js` exists.
- It owns:
  - state machine: `READY`, `PLAYING`, `PAUSED`, `GAME_OVER`, `WAVE_CLEAR`
  - per-frame input
  - player
  - formation
  - bullets/bombs
  - collision
  - spawners
  - scoring
  - VFX
  - HUD
- It should now use public `ScoreSystem.addScore(...)`.
- It still needs runtime verification that:
  - HUD/Screens callbacks are wired.
  - Bunker meshes are added to scene.
  - all VFX systems are triggered.
  - collision handling consumes/releases correct projectile references.
  - state transitions update UI correctly.

**Facade / entry status**
- `src/Space_Invaders/index.js` exists and is resolved by build.
- `src/main.js` exists.
- `src/registry.js` exists and maps `Space_Invaders` to facade.
- Facade should expose:
  - `start(container)`
  - `stop()`
- Facade should wire:
  - renderer
  - loop
  - input
  - game
  - HUD
  - screens
  - audio
  - VFX
  - dispose cascade via `ResourceTracker`

**Immediate next steps**
1. Read full current files before editing:
   - `src/Space_Invaders/index.js`
   - `src/Space_Invaders/SpaceInvadersGame.js`
   - `src/Space_Invaders/ui/HUD.js`
   - `src/Space_Invaders/ui/Screens.js`
   - `src/main.js`
   - `src/registry.js`
2. Verify facade:
   - `start(container)` creates renderer, scene, camera, composer, game, HUD, screens, audio, VFX.
   - `stop()` disposes everything through `ResourceTracker`.
   - No duplicate listeners or RAF loops.
3. Verify orchestrator:
   - state transitions update HUD/screens.
   - all six VFX systems are triggered:
     - camera shake
     - particle bursts
     - hit-stop
     - motion trails
     - shockwave rings
     - floating score text
   - Bunker meshes are added to scene.
   - power-ups fall in +z and can be collected.
   - collision events release correct pooled projectiles.
4. Run and playtest:
   - `npm run dev`
   - start screen appears.
   - Enter/start works.
   - player moves with WASD/arrows and gamepad.
   - firing works.
   - invaders step, drop, speed up.
   - bombs fire.
   - bunkers erode.
   - UFO appears and can be killed.
   - power-ups drop and apply.
   - combo builds/resets.
   - wave clear advances.
   - player death decrements lives.
   - game over and restart work.
   - pause works.
   - hi-score persists.
   - console clean.
   - stop/dispose cascade works without leaks or errors.

**Constraints to preserve**
- No placeholder code.
- No external assets.
- No physics engine.
- All materials `MeshStandardMaterial`.
- Pooling for projectiles/entities/particles where appropriate.
- Particle cap remains hard at 500.
- All disposables tracked and disposed.
- All six required VFX systems active.
- Bloom remains tuned, not maxed.
- Only Space Invaders implemented.
- Game must be playable end-to-end, not merely compilable.

## 1. Core Gameplay — Mathematical Model

### 1.1 Coordinate & Playfield Model
- Playfield is a **2D plane in (x, z)**; `y` is purely visual height. Camera sits at elevation ≈ 32°, looking down the field — classic side-view gameplay in a 3D perspective arena.
- Bounds: `X ∈ [−11, 11]`, `Z ∈ [−16 (invader line) , +14 (player line)]`.
- All collision is **AABB in XZ** — no rotation in gameplay space, so no SAT needed.

### 1.2 Invader Formation (the heart of the game)
- Grid: **5 rows × 11 columns = 55 invaders**. Cell pitch `DX = 1.55`, `DZ = 1.35`.
- Invader position: `x = fx + (c − 5)·DX`, `z = fz − (2 − r)·DZ` (row 0 = far/top, row 4 = near).
- **Discrete stepping** (authentic): `acc += dt · stepsPerSecond(remaining)`; while `acc ≥ 1`: `acc −= 1; fx += dir·STEP (0.62); frame = 1 − frame`.
- **Speed curve** (classic-inspired, piecewise-linear on remaining count `n`):

| remaining | 55 | 40 | 25 | 10 | 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| steps/s | 1.0 | 2.5 | 4.5 | 7.0 | 10.0 |

  `stepsPerSecond(n) = lerp over table × (1 + 0.15·(wave−1))`.
- **Edge + drop:** track live `minCol/maxCol`. If `dir>0` and `fx + (maxCol−5)·DX > 11` → `dir = −1; fz += DROP (1.1)`. Mirror for left.
- **Invasion condition:** any live invader `z ≥ 12.5` → player destroyed (game over), authentic to the original.
- **March audio is step-driven:** each step plays the next of 4 descending bass notes — tempo *is* the speed curve.

### 1.3 Invader Bombs
- Fire timer: `interval = lerp(1.9s, 0.45s, 1 − n/55) / (1 + 0.1·(wave−1))`.
- Each shot: pick a **random live invader, weighted toward the bottom row** (weights `[1,1,2,3,5]`); bomb `vz = +lerp(6, 14, 1 − n/55) + 2·(wave−1)` u/s.
- Bomb pool cap: 12 concurrent.

### 1.4 Player
- `x += axisX · 14 u/s · dt`, clamped to `[−10.4, 10.4]`.
- **Fire:** max 2 bullets on screen (classic constraint, modern feel), cooldown `0.28s`; power-ups raise to 3 / halve cooldown.
- Bullet: `vz = −34 u/s`, despawn at `z < −17`.
- **Tunneling-proof collision:** bullets are fast vs. small targets → **segment-vs-AABB slab test** (ray-AABB) from previous to current position, not point-in-box. Same test for bombs.

### 1.5 Bunkers (destructible shields)
- 4 bunkers at `x ∈ {−8.25, −2.75, 2.75, 8.25}`, `z = +8.5`.
- Each = **16×12 voxel grid**, cell `0.28` units. Silhouette mask computed analytically: dome top (`y > h·(1 − 0.55·(1 − (2x/w)²))`), notch at bottom center (`|x| < 0.22w && y < 0.3h → dead`).
- **Erosion:** a bullet segment passing through kills every live cell whose center is within `r = 0.55` of the segment (point-segment distance); bombs use `r = 0.95`. Bullet is consumed on first bunker contact (authentic).
- Render: **one InstancedMesh**, 4×192 = 768 box instances; dead cells get zero-scale matrices (dirty-flag batched update).

### 1.6 UFO (Mystery Ship)
- Spawns every `12–20s` (seeded RNG) when none active; crosses at `z = −14.5`, `v = ±8 u/s`.
- Score: weighted pick from `{50:40%, 100:25%, 150:15%, 300:12%, 500:8%}`.

### 1.7 Scoring, Combo, Lives, Waves
- Row values (top→bottom): **40 / 30 / 20 / 10 / 50** (classic squid/crab/octopus/small/big).
- **Combo (modern):** consecutive kills without a *missed* bullet (left field or hit bunker) raise multiplier `×1 → ×4` in 0.25 steps; any miss resets. Shown in HUD.
- Extra life at 1,000, then every 5,000. Hi-score persisted to `localStorage`.
- 3 lives; on hit: explosion, 2.0s respawn invulnerability (blink), continue.
- **Wave clear** → interstitial → next wave: formation starts `1.2` units lower, speed ×1.15, bomb rate ×1.1.

### 1.8 Power-ups (modern layer, 12% drop chance on kill)
`DOUBLE` (3s, 3 bullets) · `RAPID` (5s, cooldown ×0.5) · `SHIELD` (absorbs 1 hit, 8s) · `WIDE` (3s, 2.5× bullet hitbox). Fall at `2.2 u/s`; collect on overlap.

### 3.1 Post-processing stack
```
RenderPass

```

- Fake grounding: radial-gradient blob-shadow planes under player/invaders/UFO (transparent `MeshStandardMaterial`, opacity 0.3).

### 3.3 Procedural generation math
- **Grid texture:** 512² canvas; minor lines every 32px `rgba(0,240,255,0.55)` + `shadowBlur 6`; major every 128px magenta `rgba(255,43,214,0.8)`.
- **Particle sprite:** radial gradient `#fff → color → transparent` (used only where a texture is needed; particles themselves are geometry).
- **Invader silhouettes:** box compositions per type (e.g., squid = body box + 2 head boxes + 4 leg boxes; frame B shifts legs ±0.12), merged per frame.
- **Bunker mask:** analytic dome + notch (§1.5).
- **Retro sun:** radial gradient + `clearRect` stripe bands.
- **Seeded RNG:** mulberry32 — reproducible wave layouts/spawns per seed.

### 3.4 Draw-call budget (steady state)
Floor 1 · Sun 1 · Stars 1 · Walls 2 · Invaders 10 · Bullets 1 · Bombs 1 · Bunkers 1 · UFO 1 · Player 1 · Particles ≤4 · Rings ≤3 · Trails ≤5 · Shadows ≤3 → **≈ 35–40 draw calls**. Comfortable.

## 4. VFX Implementation — Priority Logic

**Priority order (highest wins when budget/attention conflicts):**
`PLAYER_HIT > UFO_KILL > WAVE_CLEAR > INVADER_KILL > BUNKER_EROSION > BULLET_IMPACT > AMBIENT`

| Event | Hit-stop (duration @ timescale) | Shake trauma added | Particles | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Player hit | 140 ms @ 0.05 | +0.65 | 60 sparks (white/cyan) + big shockwave | HUD red flash, engine cut |
| Player death (final) | 250 ms @ 0.03 | +0.9 | 90 sparks + double shockwave | slow-mo into game-over |
| UFO kill | 160 ms @ 0.08 | +0.45 | 40 gold sparks + shockwave | floating score (gold) |
| Invader kill | 45 ms @ 0.25 (only if combo ≥ 3) | +0.10 + 0.02·combo | 22 sparks (type color) + ring | floating `+N×M` text |
| Bomb hits bunker | — | +0.06 | 12 sparks | crater |
| Bullet hits bunker | — | +0.03 | 8 sparks | — |
| Power-up pickup | 60 ms @ 0.4 | +0.05 | 16 sparks (type color) | chime + HUD tag |
| Wave clear | 200 ms @ 0.1 | +0.3 | 80 sparks across formation | fanfare + interstitial |

- **Hit-stop** is a **global timescale** on the fixed-timestep accumulator (physics, particles, trails all dilate uniformly; render keeps running) — reads as *weight*, never stutter.
- **Shake** is trauma-based: `trauma = min(1, trauma + add)`, decay `e^(−3.2·dt)`, offset `trauma²·0.55` in a 2-axis pseudo-noise; applied post-parallax so it never fights the camera follow.
- **Particle budget:** manager enforces 500 hard; over-cap spawns recycle the oldest instance (ring buffer), so a wave-clear burst can never starve a later player-hit burst — priority is enforced by *size*, not by dropping.

_nearestParticleColor(hex) {
  const colors = [0x00f0ff, 0xff2bd6, 0xffd166, 0xffffff];
  const r = (hex >> 16) & 255, g = (hex >> 8) & 255, b = hex & 255;
  let best = colors[0], bestD = Infinity;
  for (const c of colors) {
    const cr = (c >> 16) & 255, cg = (c >> 8) & 255, cb = c & 255;
    const d = (r-cr)**2 + (g-cg)**2 + (b-cb)**2;
    if (d < bestD) { bestD = d; best = c; }
  }
  return best;
}

**Hand-off note — Space Invaders implementation in progress**

**Mission / user request**
- Build exactly one playable AAA retro-futurism game from the provided collection.
- User selected: **Space Invaders**.
- Required stack: Three.js vanilla ES modules, Vite, no external game/physics engines, 100% procedural assets, `MeshStandardMaterial`, glassmorphism HTML/CSS UI, keyboard + gamepad input.
- Mandatory performance/quality constraints: object pooling, hard 500-particle cap, `InstancedMesh`/merged geometry where applicable, explicit `.dispose()` memory management, no placeholder code, all imports must resolve, all called methods must exist.
- Required VFX: camera shake, particle bursts, hit-stop, motion trails, shockwave rings, floating score text.
- Required post-processing: `EffectComposer` + `UnrealBloomPass`, tuned so emissive surfaces glow without washing out.
- Definition of done: game launches, responds to input, core loop reaches win/loss, playable end-to-end.

**Workflow state**
- STEP 1 completed: master architecture presented as text only.
- User said: **“Begin Space Invaders”**.
- STEP 2 completed: detailed `plan.md` for Space Invaders presented.
- User said: **“Plan approved”**.
- STEP 3 is in progress: implementation started.
- Workspace was initially empty.
- Environment checked: Node `v22.19.0`, npm `10.9.3`, npm registry reachable.
- Pinned versions chosen: `three@0.186.0`, `vite@8.3.0`.

**Locked architecture decisions**
- One isolated game folder: `src/Space_Invaders/`.
- Reusable shared layer: `src/shared/`.
- Vite aliases:
  - `@` → `src/`
  - `@shared` → `src/shared/`
- No deep relative imports.
- Shared code is reusable across future games, but only Space Invaders is implemented.
- `src/main.js` and `src/registry.js` are intended entry/registry files, but they have not been shown as written yet.
- Game facade will own lifecycle and dispose cascade.
- Fixed-timestep simulation at 120 Hz, render at display rate.
- Hit-stop is implemented as global timescale dilation, not per-entity pause.
- Particle cap is structural: centralized `ParticleManager` with hard cap 500, oldest-recycled over cap.
- Bloom settings from plan:
  - strength `0.85`
  - radius `0.55`
  - threshold `0.72`
- Tone mapping: ACES filmic, sRGB output.
- No shadow maps; fake blob shadows used for grounding.
- All gameplay collision is 2D in XZ using AABB / segment-AABB slab tests.
- No rotation in gameplay space.

**Space Invaders design facts**
- Playfield:
  - X bounds roughly `[-11, 11]`.
  - Z from invader line near `-16` to player line near `+14`.
  - Invasion/game-over if any live invader reaches `z >= 12.5`.
- Invader formation:
  - 5 rows × 11 columns = 55 invaders.
  - Cell pitch: `DX = 1.55`, `DZ = 1.35`.
  - Discrete stepping, not continuous movement.
  - Step size: `0.62`.
  - Drop size: `1.1`.
  - Speed increases as remaining count decreases.
  - Wave scaling: speed ×1.15 per wave, bomb rate ×1.1 per wave, formation starts lower.
- Invader bombs:
  - Max concurrent bombs: 12.
  - Fire interval decreases as invaders die.
  - Targeting weighted toward bottom rows.
- Player:
  - Movement speed: `14 u/s`.
  - X clamp: `[-10.4, 10.4]`.
  - Max bullets on screen: 2 normally, 3 with DOUBLE power-up.
  - Fire cooldown: `0.28s`, halved with RAPID.
  - Bullet speed: `vz = -34 u/s`.
  - Bullet despawn: `z < -17`.
- Bunkers:
  - 4 bunkers at `x = -8.25, -2.75, 2.75, 8.25`, `z = 8.5`.
  - Each bunker: 16×12 voxel grid.
  - Cell size: `0.28`.
  - Dome silhouette with bottom notch.
  - Erosion by projectile segment distance.
  - Bullet bunker erosion radius: `0.55`.
  - Bomb bunker erosion radius: `0.95`.
  - Bullet consumed on first bunker contact.
- UFO:
  - Spawns every 12–20 seconds when inactive.
  - Crosses at `z = -14.5`.
  - Speed: `±8 u/s`.
  - Weighted score: 50 / 100 / 150 / 300 / 500.
- Scoring:
  - Row values top to bottom: `40 / 30 / 20 / 10 / 50`.
  - Combo multiplier: ×1 to ×4.
  - Combo resets on missed bullet.
  - Extra life at 1,000, then every 5,000.
  - Hi-score persisted to `localStorage`.
- Power-ups:
  - Drop chance: 12%.

history.summary:
**Hand-off note — Space Invaders implementation**

**Mission**
- Build exactly one playable AAA retro-futurism game: **Space Invaders**.
- Stack: Three.js vanilla ES modules, Vite, no game/physics engines, 100% procedural assets, `MeshStandardMaterial`, glassmorphism UI, keyboard + gamepad.
- Hard constraints: object pooling, 500-particle cap, `InstancedMesh`/merged geometry where applicable, explicit `.dispose()` cascade, no placeholders, all imports/methods must resolve.
- Required VFX: camera shake, particle bursts, hit-stop, motion trails, shockwave rings, floating score text.
- Required post: `EffectComposer` + `UnrealBloomPass`, tuned not maxed.
- Done = launches, input works, core loop reaches win/loss, playable end-to-end.

**Current workflow state**
- Architecture and `plan.md` approved.
- Shared layer complete.
- Space Invaders config, scene builder, and entity layer complete.
- Orchestrator `SpaceInvadersGame.js` written and partially fixed.
- Systems, UI, facade, and root entry files are not complete.
- Files are on disk; verify by reading, not assuming.

**Locked architecture**
- Game folder: `src/Space_Invaders/`.
- Shared folder: `src/shared/`.
- Aliases: `@` → `src/`, `@shared` → `src/shared/`.
- Fixed-timestep simulation at 120 Hz; render at display rate.
- Hit-stop = global timescale dilation.
- Particle cap = centralized `ParticleManager`, hard 500, oldest recycled.
- Bloom: strength `0.85`, radius `0.55`, threshold `0.72`.
- ACES tone mapping, sRGB output.
- No shadow maps; fake blob shadows.
- Gameplay collision is 2D XZ using AABB / segment-AABB.
- No gameplay rotation.

**Key design facts**
- Playfield: X roughly `[-11, 11]`, Z from invader line near `-16` to player near `+14`.
- Invasion/game over if live invader reaches `z >= 12.5`.
- Formation: 5 rows × 11 columns = 55 invaders.
- Invader movement: discrete stepping, step `0.62`, drop `1.1`, speed increases as count decreases.
- Wave scaling: speed ×1.15, bomb rate ×1.1, formation starts lower.
- Player: speed `14 u/s`, X clamp `[-10.4, 10.4]`, max bullets 2 normally / 3 with DOUBLE, cooldown `0.28s`, bullet `vz = -34`, despawn `z < -17`.
- Bunkers: 4 at `x = -8.25, -2.75, 2.75, 8.25`, `z = 8.5`; 16×12 voxel grid, cell `0.28`; erosion by projectile segment distance.
- UFO: spawns every 12–20s, crosses at `z = -14.5`, speed `±8 u/s`, score 50/100/150/300/500.
- Scoring: row values top-to-bottom `40/30/20/10/50`, combo ×1–×4, extra life at 1000 then every 5000, hi-score in `localStorage`.
- Power-ups: 12% drop chance, types `DOUBLE`, `RAPID`, `SHIELD`, `WIDE`, fall speed `2.2 u/s`.
- Hit-stop values:
  - player hit: 140 ms @ 0.05
  - player death: 250 ms @ 0.03
  - UFO kill: 160 ms @ 0.08
  - invader kill: 45 ms @ 0.25 only if combo ≥ 3
  - power-up pickup: 60 ms @ 0.4
  - wave clear: 200 ms @ 0.1

**Build:** `npm run build` passes (38 JS files, 57 modules, 173ms). The >500 kB chunk warning is expected (Three.js + all procedural assets in one bundle) and not a blocker.

**Runtime playtest (Playwright, real browser):** I drove the actual game through every state and system. Zero JavaScript errors across the entire session — the only console entries are favicon 404s.

- **Boot → Start** — start screen renders, "Start" button and Enter both launch into PLAYING (3 lives, wave 1, 55 invaders).
- **Player movement** — A/D and arrows move the ship, clamped to ±10.4.
- **Firing** — Space fires pooled bullets (max 2 on screen), with motion trails.
- **Invader kills** — bullets travel, hit the formation, score (60 from 2 kills), trigger particle bursts, shockwave rings, floating score text, and combo-scaled hit-stop.
- **Bombs** — invaders fire; bomb hits drain lives (3 → 0) with the full death VFX cascade.
- **Game over** — lives reaching 0 shows the game-over screen with score/hi-score/wave; "Play Again" restarts cleanly.
- **Hi-score** — persists to `localStorage` (`neon_invaders_hi`).
- **Pause/resume** — P toggles PAUSED with the pause screen; resumes correctly.
- **Wave clear** — emptying the formation shows the wave-clear screen, then auto-advances to wave 2 with a fresh 55-invader formation.
- **Power-ups** — RAPID pickup applies (cooldown halves 0.28 → 0.14, timer counts down).
